title: Netanyahu orders full lockdown of West Bank after shooting; Bombshell report on Kushner’s $2B slush fund; Brent crude hits $114
author: Drop Site News
content:
**Friday, October 23, 2026 -**_****_

_**Iran** : President Donald Trump accuses Iran of driving up oil prices as
Brent crude hits $114. Europe faces winter energy crisis, International Energy
Agency chief warns. U.S. spent $11 billion in three years defending Israel,
analysis finds. United Arab Emirates closes Umm Al Quwain beaches after oil
spill from tanker. U.S. claims naval blockade prevented Iran from exporting
$25 billion in oil over 100 days._

_**Palestine** : Three Palestinians killed, several wounded in Israeli strikes
across Gaza. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu orders full closure of
the occupied West Bank after Hebron shooting. Israeli settlers and soldiers
rampage across the West Bank. Israeli settlers destroy late Palestinian-
American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh memorial._

_**Yemen** : Ansarallah claims Saudi Arabia rejected five-day ceasefire
proposal for talks. Saudi-led coalition launches strikes across Yemen as Saudi
Arabia intercepts Ansarallah missiles._

_**Lebanon** : Israeli airstrikes, artillery shelling reported in southern
Lebanon despite ceasefire._

_**U.S.** : Jared Kushner received $2 billion in dark money from Gulf States,
new book excerpt alleges. CBS: Hegseth bans Pentagon personnel from using
nonpublic information to bet on U.S. military operations. ProPublica: Postal
Service cuts cause sharp rise in ballot rejections during midterms. Judge
restricts DHS investigations of supposed noncitizen voting. WSJ: DOJ
corruption probe examines Corey Lewandowski. DOJ charges 15 in health care
fraud worth nearly $2 billion. Musk gives another $76 million to America PAC;
his total midterm donations now $442+ million. Axios: Major U.S. banks
discover third-party AI agents in customer accounts. Ohio governor's race now
"leans Democratic," per analysis. Virginia state senator charged with
conspiracy, bribery, racketeering._

_**International:** Egypt editor faces trial in escalated press crackdown. Six
killed, 28 wounded in church funeral shooting in Jordan. Sudanese army strikes
Darfur, Kordofan. Mob beats immigrant to death in South Africa. WHO says Ebola
outbreak is becoming "more complex"; infections in three African countries.
Syria security force raids suspected ISIS cell; seven dead. Hundreds flee
Ethiopia fighting for Kenya. Tunisian police fire tear gas at protesters after
detainee's death. Major earthquake kills 16 in Tibet. Musk restores Ukraine's
Starlink access, Trump says. 10,000+ rally in student-led protest against
Serbia's ruling party on eve of election. Germany arrests Ukrainian national
on suspicion of spying for Russia._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Iran

  * **Trump accuses Iran of driving up oil prices as Brent crude hits $114:** President Donald Trump accused Iran of deliberately attempting to raise global oil prices ahead of the November midterm elections.

    * "Iran is doing everything they can to drive up the price of Oil prior to the U.S. Midterm Election," Trump [wrote](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/117485314798987090) on Truth Social. "They are even making up fake hits, mines, and everything else," he claimed, insisting that more oil is now passing through the Strait of Hormuz than before the war began.

    * Middle East Gulf and Gulf of Oman oil and petroleum product exports, excluding Iran, [fell](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2113460339698278486) to around 15 million barrels per day (bpd) on a seven-day moving average, down from a pre-war baseline of 20.5 million bpd, according to Kpler data. Kpler says data from the past two weeks may be revised upward.

    * Brent crude [hit](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2113500628802478318) a high of $114.72 overnight. The U.S. national average price for regular gasoline sits at $4.284 per gallon, a 5-cent drop from last week; diesel fuel now averages $6.276 per gallon, a 10-cent increase.

  * **Europe faces winter energy crisis, IEA chief warns:** Europe is entering winter with historically low natural gas reserves and cannot withstand further supply disruptions caused by the U.S. war with Iran, the International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol [warned](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/10/23/eu-entering-winter-with-lowest-gas-reserves-on-record-iea-boss-warns).

    * EU gas storage is just 72% full, compared with the usual 90% ahead of winter, a shortfall equivalent to the energy needs of 10 to 12 million homes. Nearly 10% of Europe's liquefied natural gas previously passed through the Strait of Hormuz, where attacks on vessels have disrupted shipping.

    * "Life will not be easy for Europe this year and also next year," Birol told Al Jazeera, adding that even an immediate ceasefire would not prevent higher energy costs in the coming months. Birol also warned of diesel shortages linked to Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries.

    * "I have never ever seen the dark and long shadow of geopolitics so dominant in the energy sector," Birol said. "Energy is not currently considered a business but a political leverage."

  * **U.S. spent $11 billion in three years defending Israel, analysis finds:** The U.S. fired an estimated 609 missile interceptors to defend Israeli territory between October 2023 and June 2026, costing approximately $11 billion in taxpayer money, according to an [analysis](https://www.stephensemler.com/p/us-fired-over-600-missile-interceptors) by researcher Stephen Semler. The estimate excludes interceptors fired to defend U.S. forces in the region.

    * "That is not a symbiotic relationship. It is a parasitic one," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [wrote](https://x.com/araghchi/status/2113506676946911570?s=46) on X, sharing the analysis.

  * **UAE closes Umm Al Quwain beaches after oil spill from tanker:** The UAE [temporarily closed](https://x.com/moccaeuae/status/2113390299598721449?s=46) all beaches and coastal areas in Umm Al Quwain after an oil spill from a tanker contaminated the shoreline.

    * The spill comes amid escalating Iranian attacks on commercial vessels and oil tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz. UAE authorities did not link the spill to the war. Other regional spills, including oil slicks near Iran's Qeshm and Hengam islands and along Oman's coastline, were caused by attacks on vessels in the region.

  * **U.S. claims naval blockade prevented Iran from exporting $25 billion in oil over 100 days:** The naval blockade of Iran prevented at least $25 billion worth of Iranian crude oil exports since it resumed 100 days ago, CENTCOM claimed in a [post](https://x.com/centcom/status/2113328696153215144?s=46) on X. CENTCOM claimed that due to the blockade, dubbed "America's steel wall," no goods have entered or left Iran by sea, except for "humanitarian shipments U.S. forces have allowed."

# Palestine

  * **Three Palestinians killed, several wounded in Israeli strikes across Gaza:** Two Palestinians were killed and others wounded on Friday in an Israeli [airstrike](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/23/%D8%B4%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%86-%D9%88%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%AC%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%84%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D8%BA%D8%B1%D8%A8-%D9%85%D8%AF%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%A9) on the Al-Nasr neighborhood of western Gaza City, according to WAFA.

    * In southern Gaza, an Israeli drone strike targeting a bicycle on Al-Qubba Street, west of Khan Younis, killed one Palestinian and wounded others.

  * **Netanyahu orders full closure of West Bank after Hebron shooting:** Two Palestinian gunmen [opened fire](https://www.timesofisrael.com/5-injured-2-critically-in-west-bank-shooting-idf-believes-gunmen-planned-larger-attack/) at an Israeli military checkpoint near Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday, killing two Israeli soldiers and wounding three others before being killed by Israeli forces. The gunfight lasted more than 20 minutes.

    * Israeli forces then imposed a sweeping military lockdown on Hebron governorate, closing all entrances and exits, and preventing Palestinian movement. Troops raided homes and [detained](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/23/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-%D8%AB%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AB%D8%A9-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%86-%D9%85%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AE%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%84) at least five Palestinians in raids, according to WAFA. Israeli forces also [critically wounded](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/23/%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A9-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%B5-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%AF%D9%88%D8%B1%D8%A7-%D8%AC%D9%86%D9%88%D8%A8-%D8%BA%D8%B1%D8%A8) a Palestinian driver after shooting him in the chest in Dura, southwest of Hebron, and closed the Ibrahimi Mosque to Muslim worshippers.

    * During a subsequent visit to Hebron on Friday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced he had instructed the army and security forces to "immediately impose a closure on the city of Hebron" and prepare for a "full lockdown" of the entire West Bank starting Friday.

    * Netanyahu added that along with Defense Minister Israel Katz they were considering an extensive operation in the West Bank "such as has not been carried out since the Six Day War," in reference to 1967.

    * Netanyahu announced plans to apply the same "successful and aggressive model" used in the occupied West Bank refugee camps, where Israeli forces have displaced tens of thousands of residents and demolished large areas in what rights groups [have said](https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/11/20/west-bank-israel-emptying-refugee-camps-a-crime-against-humanity) are crimes against humanity.

  * **Israeli settlers and soldiers rampage across the occupied West Bank:**

    * **Ramallah:** Settlers [burned and cut down](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/23/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D8%AD%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%88%D9%8A%D9%82%D8%B7%D8%B9%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B9%D8%B4%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A3%D8%B4%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%86) dozens of olive trees in the Al-Qibla area south of Burqa on Friday, WAFA reported. In Sinjil, settlers attacked olive harvesters and broke branches off fruit-bearing trees.

    * **Nablus:** Israeli forces [fired](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/23/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%AA%D8%B3%D8%A8%D8%A8-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%AF%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B9-%D8%AD%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%82-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%B3%D9%87%D9%84%D9%8A-%D8%B3%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85) tear gas canisters toward Palestinians in the agricultural plains of Salem and Beit Furik, igniting fires. In Burin, settlers attempted to set fire to a Palestinian home and its surroundings under Israeli military protection.

    * **Jenin:** Israeli forces gave families in Khirbet Suruj one week to evacuate their homes and agricultural structures. The community includes more than seven homes and ten livestock sheds, with families who have lived there since 1950 and hold land documents dating back to 1960.

    * **East** **Jerusalem:** Israeli forces [arrested](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/23/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%84-%D8%AE%D8%B7%D9%8A%D8%A8-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AC%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%82%D8%B5%D9%89-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B4%D9%8A%D8%AE-%D8%AE%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AF) Sheikh Khaled Abu Jumaa, the Al-Aqsa Mosque preacher, after he delivered the Friday sermon and led prayers at the mosque.

  * **Israeli settlers destroy Shireen Abu Akleh memorial:** Armed settlers [destroyed](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/10/23/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D8%AD%D8%B7%D9%85%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%86%D8%B5%D8%A8%D8%A7-%D8%AA%D8%B0%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A7-%D9%84%D9%84%D8%B4%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%88) a memorial to Palestinian-American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh near the entrance to the village of Ajja south of Jenin city. The memorial was erected in 2022 to honor the Al Jazeera journalist, who was shot in the head and killed by Israeli forces while covering a military raid on Jenin refugee camp on May 11, 2022.

# Yemen

  * **Ansarallah claims Saudi Arabia rejected five-day ceasefire proposal for talks:** Senior Ansarallah official Mohammed Al-Bukhaiti [said](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2113481406009458964) that while Riyadh sought mediation through Oman during the initial escalation in July, Saudi Arabia did not accept a proposed five-day ceasefire for direct talks. In an interview with The Grayzone's Max Blumenthal, Al-Bukhaiti said that Ansarallah had agreed to the proposal.

    * Al-Bukhaiti claimed Ansarallah forces captured Mount Han overlooking Taiz, the major southwestern city under siege, while insisting that any future peace agreement end the war and blockades imposed by both sides.

    * He also called on Saudi Arabia's ruling family to oust Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, saying his continued rule threatens the kingdom itself. "We will support any move within the ruling family … to oust bin Salman," he said, urging action by Saudi citizens and opposition groups.

  * **Saudi-led coalition launches strikes across Yemen as Saudi Arabia intercepts Ansarallah missiles:** At least 18 airstrikes were reported across Yemen's Saada, Hodeidah, Al-Jawf, Amran, and Taiz governorates, according to Ansarallah-affiliated media.

    * **Saudi Arabia:** Air defenses intercepted and destroyed ballistic missiles launched by Ansarallah toward Riyadh and Khamis Mushait, in southwestern Saudi Arabia, Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki said.

# Lebanon

  * **Israeli airstrikes, artillery shelling reported in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire:** Israeli warplanes [carried out](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/570090/%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D9%85%D8%AD%D9%8A%D8%B7-%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A9-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B7%D8%A7%D9%87%D8%B1-2) an airstrike near Ali Al-Taher Hill, while intermittent Israeli artillery shelling targeted the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiya on Friday in the Nabatieh district, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

    * In the Marjayoun district, Israeli forces reportedly [set fire](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/570029/%D9%82%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%AF%D9%88-%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A5%D8%AD%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%82-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AC-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82%D9%86%D8%B7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%84%D8%AC%D9%87%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%84%D9%88%D9%82%D9%8A-2) to wooded areas in the town of Qantara.

# U.S. News

  * **Jared Kushner received $2 billion in dark money from Gulf States:** U.S. special envoy and Trump son-in-law **Jared Kushner** received $2 billion in a slush fund created by top Emirati and Saudi officials, according to an [excerpt](https://www.vanityfair.com/story/jared-kushner-hacked-phone-secret-negotiations) of a new book by investigative reporter **Matthew Cole**. Cole reports an extraordinary sequence of events that began with Russian intelligence infiltrating Kushner's iPhone. According to Cole, Dutch intelligence captured a Russian agent, flipped him, and gained access to Kushner's device themselves. As they began to monitor Kushner's phone in real time, they observed suspicious transfers of huge amounts of money.

    * According to Cole, UAE ruler **Mohamed bin Zayed** and**** Saudi Crown Prince **Mohammed bin Salman** sought to influence U.S. foreign policy during the first Trump term, and offered Kushner the money toward that end.

    * The arrangement also involved Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who directed Kushner in 2018 to set up an account at the Israeli Central Bank. Netanyahu reportedly required Kushner to inform him before moving any money out of the account.

    * Kushner denied Cole's reporting as "categorically false" and "completely insane" in a [statement](https://x.com/jaredkushner/status/2113373330170368450) on Thursday. Through his attorney, Kushner said he would [pursue](https://x.com/chad_mizelle/status/2113418286092194022) legal action against the publisher of Cole's book, Simon & Schuster.

    * The full excerpt from the book published in Vanity Fair is available [here](https://www.vanityfair.com/story/jared-kushner-hacked-phone-secret-negotiations?srsltid=AYCX9vLlmfavzNCoA0AFGzxfKo-jeY2mdYeXv5eDjieUn3x_BT04Krig). Cole's book, "Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed's Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East," will be released on October 27. It can be pre-ordered [here](https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Princes-and-Thieves/Matthew-Cole/9781668095324).

  * **CBS: Hegseth bans Pentagon personnel from using nonpublic information to bet on U.S. military operations:** War Secretary **Pete Hegseth** barred department personnel from using classified or unclassified nonpublic information to bet on military operations, he wrote in an October 20 memo to senior Pentagon leaders and combatant commanders that was [obtained](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/hegseth-betting-ban-military-operations/) by CBS News. The memo names prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi, and says that violations could bring administrative discipline or criminal action under federal law or the Uniform Code of Military Justice.

    * The directive follows scrutiny of military-related betting. In April, Army Master Sgt. **Gannon Ken Van Dyke** , a Special Forces soldier involved in the operation that captured **Nicol as Maduro**, was arrested for allegedly betting more than $33,000 on Polymarket on Maduro's removal within hours of President Trump's January announcement, winning more than $409,000. He pleaded not guilty in federal court in New York.

  * **ProPublica: Postal Service cuts cause sharp rise in ballot rejections during midterms:** In counties where the Postal Service reduced pickups from twice a day to once a day in rural areas, late-ballot rejection rates were two or three times higher than they were in 2022, ProPublica [reported](https://www.propublica.org/article/mail-ballot-delays-postal-service-midterms). In 11 rural counties of Washington, for instance, nearly 2,000 ballots arrived late this year, compared to about 600 in 2022.

  * **Judge restricts DHS investigations of supposed noncitizen voting:** U.S. District Judge **Araceli Mart inez-Olguin** [halted](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/22/judge-blocks-dhs-investigations-noncitizen-voting-citing-flawed-data/) portions of the Department of Homeland Security's aggressive investigations of supposed noncitizens. The order bars the DHS from stopping or interviewing suspects in nine states. The judge found the plaintiffs--including National Nurses United and Voto Latino--likely to succeed in their claim that the DHS investigations infringe upon the Voting Rights Act. "The public's interest in safe elections, free from interference or intimidation," she [wrote](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.cand.479338/gov.uscourts.cand.479338.87.0.pdf), "far exceed defendants' purported interest in combating unlawful voting by non-U.S. citizens."

  * **WSJ: DOJ corruption probe examines Corey Lewandowski:** The Justice Department is [examining](https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/corey-lewandowski-doj-investigation-a6ccde19) whether **Corey Lewandowski** , top adviser to then-Homeland Security Secretary **Kristi Noem** , profited from his political position, the Wall Street Journal [reported](https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/corey-lewandowski-doj-investigation-a6ccde19). The inquiry rests on a recent referral from the DHS inspector general. It focuses, in part, on contracting fraud. The review is the first publicly known instance of Trump's second-term DOJ scrutinizing someone close to the president. Investigators found evidence Lewandowski may have been involved in improperly awarding contracts. He or his close associates approved almost all spending above $100,000, and he personally signed contracts despite serving as an unpaid Special Government Employee. Lewandowski, through a representative, denied wrongdoing.

  * **DOJ charges 15 in health care fraud worth nearly $2 billion:** The Justice Department [charged](https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-10-22/california-federal-health-care-fraud-charges) 15 defendants, including six medical professionals, with luring vulnerable patients into needless surgeries, sham treatment programs, and bogus hospice care. In one case, two people allegedly paid Texas "body brokers" to recruit homeless people and 12-step participants into sham California sober living homes, where they were signed up for pricey insurance and then left to languish in "decrepit squats." In another case, three people allegedly pressured healthy seniors into hospice care.

  * **Musk gives another $76 million to America PAC; his total midterm donations now $442+ million** : **Elon Musk** [gave](https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/10/22/congress/more-musk-money-01133454) $76 million to his super PAC, America PAC, in the first two weeks of October, pushing his total donations above $442 million this election cycle. His giving in 2026 far exceeds the roughly $290 million he spent in 2024. Musk's earlier spending includes $158 million to the campaign arm of Senate Republicans, which was then transferred to a super PAC boosting Texas AG **Ken Paxton** in his tight race against Democrat **James Talarico**. He has given to many other groups: the House Republicans super PAC, Trump's MAGA Inc., a group seeking to repeal Alaska's ranked-choice voting, and various GOP candidates. Musk has not campaigned with GOP candidates this fall, unlike in prior years, and Republicans privately acknowledge he could be politically toxic.

  * **Axios: Major U.S. banks discover third-party AI agents in customer accounts** : Top U.S. banks are discovering unauthorized AI agents inside customer accounts, Axios [reported](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/22/ai-agents-banks-unauthorized-accounts-access) on Thursday. Most cases involve an AI agent or assistant using a customer's login credentials with their permission--which is still a violation of most banks' rules. But some banks have also found AI agents that contact call centers or take actions that appear independent of user instructions.

  * **Ohio governor 's race now "leans Democratic," per analysis**: The nonpartisan election newsletter Sabato's Crystal Ball [shifted](https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/the-governors-ohio-to-leans-democratic-among-other-changes-as-dems-eye-gubernatorial-majority/) the Ohio governor's race toward Democratic nominee **Amy Acton** , citing "an explosive--and desperate--attack ad" by Republican **Vivek Ramaswamy**. The ad features Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, who says, "She lies about her past. She says she grew up living in a tent. None of that is true. She's lied her entire life." Ramaswamy's campaign confirmed that it was behind the ad and said it would spend $4 million to promote it. Acton has openly discussed her experience of childhood abuse, neglect, and homelessness.

  * **Virginia state senator charged with conspiracy, bribery, racketeering:** Virginia state Senator **Louise Lucas** , 82, was [arrested](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/l-louise-lucas-charged-indictment-arrested-virginia/) on charges related to marijuana distribution, bribery, and racketeering on Thursday. Six other co-defendants were charged, including her daughters **Lisa Lucas-Burke** and **Theresa Lucas-Lamb** and her grandson **Ryan Eichelberger**. Prosecutors say that since at least 2019, Lucas led a scheme that used her political influence to enact legislation and regulations benefiting herself and co-defendants and shielding a marijuana enterprise from state law enforcement. Federal agents searched her office and The Cannabis Outlet, a shop she co-owns, nearly six months ago, and the investigation reportedly began under President **Joe Biden**.

# Other International News

  * **Egypt editor faces trial in escalated press crackdown:** Lina Attalah, the editor-in-chief of Mada Masr, one of Egypt's last remaining independent media outlets, was referred to trial on Thursday. The escalation comes one day after prosecutors questioned her for more than six hours. Rights groups describe her case as an unprecedented attack on press freedoms in Egypt.

    * The Supreme State Prosecution referred Attalah to trial on a charge of establishing and managing a website without a license. She was also questioned on a charge of publishing false news, but that charge was not included in her court referral.

    * Atallah was released Wednesday evening on bail of 100,000 Egyptian pounds (around $1,800). She is due in court on October 27. If convicted, she faces a fine of one million to three million Egyptian pounds (roughly $18,000 to $54,000). The court may also order the closure of Mada Masr and the confiscation of its equipment.

    * Over 100 independent media outlets and civil society organizations around the world, including Drop Site News, signed a joint [statement](https://timep.org/2026/10/23/urgent-global-call-following-the-referral-of-mada-masr-editor-in-chief-lina-attalah-to-trial/) condemning Attalah's referral to trial, calling it "an unprecedented escalation that threatens the future of the entire independent media, knowledge production, and civil society space in Egypt."

    * Drop Site News and Mada Masr have co-published several articles over the past two years.
